deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Every conclusion must show how the team reached it: evidence or hypothesis -> conclusion -> design requirement -> product response.
deck.evidence_rule: Mentor advice and team discussion can shape the pitch but do not count as participant validation. Unverified claims remain visibly labelled or blocked.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: The same appreciation sentence moves from an occasion-only social script into a deliberately made object, then reaches the room as an optional handoff card.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity before the spoken story begins.

visual.composition: Current holding state: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark alone on white. Final state: a real approved team photograph in a bespoke team composition, with confirmed team number and names.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Blocked until the team supplies and approves the real team photo, team number and member names. Do not fabricate or substitute portraits.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time you sent or received a letter, just because?
slides.audience_takeaway: Feel the contrast between how meaningful a letter can be and how rarely an ordinary day prompts one.

visual.composition: One full-frame audience question. After a pause, add the smaller counterpoint: we have never had more ways to talk.

speaker_notes: Timing: 18 seconds.
Ask both sides aloud: when did you last send one, and when did you last receive one?
Do not imply that everyone values letters or that rarity proves the problem.

motion.description: The letter question lands before the communication contradiction appears.

slides.claim: there's no expectation or norm to show appreciation for friends and family
slides.audience_takeaway: Hear Chloe's central clause directly before the team compresses it into the pitch's central rule.

visual.composition: A dedicated full-frame direct excerpt using only Chloe's exact central clause: `there's no expectation or norm to show appreciation for friends and family`. Attribute it to Chloe with a small source line and point to the complete machine transcript in the notes. Do not style it as participant research or a population finding.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
Read only the direct excerpt on screen. Do not make the audience work through the full machine-transcribed sentence.
Ethan confirmed Chloe's attribution; Chronicle assigned the full capture to Ethan, so retain the machine-transcript note.
The following slide gives the team's concise, normalized framing. Mentor guidance shapes the argument but does not validate prevalence.

motion.description: Reveal the quote once, highlighting `there's no expectation or norm to show appreciation for friends and family` as the bridge to the normalized rule.

slides.claim: Without an occasion, appreciation has no familiar social permission.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the unwritten rule: birthdays, farewells and milestones prompt appreciation; an ordinary day does not.

visual.composition: A split social script: birthdays, farewells and milestones each provide permission; an ordinary Tuesday provides no prompt. Close with the direct How Might We: How might we create that permission on an ordinary day?

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Normalized from the mentor-endorsed framing at 30:02; the dedicated preceding slide and deck/TRANSCRIPT_PRESENTATION_FINDINGS.md preserve the exact machine transcript.
Present the social rule as the team's evidence-informed working framing, not a universal population fact.

motion.description: Reveal the occasion script, remove the occasion, then reveal the How Might We.

slides.claim: We thought the gap sat between a text and a letter. The mentors made us prove it.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the team's initial format hypothesis and the evidence it still needs before it becomes a conclusion.

visual.composition: A clearly stamped TEAM HYPOTHESIS x/y field. Y is practical cost in time and money; X is perceived meaning and expressive effort. Plot text, voice note, video call, digital card/group board, gift and handwritten letter. Highlight and name `THE ORDINARY-DAY GAP`: meaningful enough to feel deliberate, low-friction enough to send today. Beside it show the intentionally blank evidence marker `___%` with the caption `matched-format participant test pending`. Never fill the number or present the gap as measured before that test.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Video call is required because the mentors identified it as a meaningful existing closeness channel missing from the first map.
Name the highlighted area `the ordinary-day gap`, then point to `___%` and say the matched-format participant test is still pending.

Every position and the gap itself remain conceptual until intended participants compare the same appreciation across text, voice or video, this digital object and a physical note. Never invent the percentage.

motion.description: Place existing methods first, then outline the unverified gap and stamp it as a hypothesis.

slides.claim: Research gave us three reasons to take the gap seriously.
slides.audience_takeaway: See how gratitude misforecasting, communication-channel effects and occasion-led card categories narrowed the problem to ordinary-day context and reply pressure.

visual.composition: Three evidence cards: gratitude-letter studies found expressers overestimated recipient awkwardness and underestimated positive response; voice-based interactions created stronger social bonds than text without more awkwardness; Hallmark and Kudoboard still organise discovery around occasion categories. Every claim carries a visible source and narrow boundary.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Keep the study boundary explicit: it concerns gratitude letters and does not prove this audience, this norm or this product.
The communication study compares voice-based and text-based interactions; it does not prove that a digital object outperforms either.
Existing product categories show how current choices are organised, not an unmet market or product advantage.

motion.description: Evidence appears first, followed by the narrower question and resulting requirement.

slides.claim: Primary evidence is the missing link.
slides.audience_takeaway: Know exactly what must be learned from the intended audience before the team claims that the opportunity or solution works.

visual.composition: Three evidence lanes, all visibly marked PENDING until completed: quantitative evidence for what and how often; qualitative evidence for why, context, interpretation and exceptions; prototype observation for where people hesitate and what changes. No fake metrics, quotes, participant photography or decorative affinity board.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.

The team-selected first market is university students maintaining long-distance connections with friends and family. State that this is a targeting decision for research and design, not evidence of demand.
Blocked until participant count, recruitment, questions, method, analysis, exceptions and exact findings are recorded.
Do not convert informal mentor discussion, team agreement or prototype enthusiasm into research evidence.

motion.description: Reveal quant, qual and observation as three separate jobs; retain pending labels.

slides.claim: Our first market: university students maintaining long-distance connections with friends and family.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the team's chosen starting audience and one illustrative end-to-end situation, without treating either as evidence of demand.

visual.composition: Lead with the team-selected market, then show a clearly stamped ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO / DEMAND UNVALIDATED using the requested grandmother and university-student granddaughter duo: an ordinary-day thought -> text feels too casual, a call needs both people free and a letter will not happen today -> one thoughtful object -> receiver opens it when ready and may keep, close or remove it. No names, ages, locations, quotes or claimed behaviour.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Say explicitly that university students maintaining long-distance friend and family connections are the team's selected first market, not a research finding.
The grandmother-granddaughter journey is illustrative, not a researched persona or demand signal.
The intended cadence is occasional and unexpected, not frequent back-and-forth and not another social network.
Do not invent names, ages, locations, motivations, quotes or behaviour.

motion.description: Move through trigger, sending, receiving and revisiting as one end-to-end situation.

slides.claim: Every conclusion had to earn a product decision.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the causal process that moved the team from a message field to a finite, authored and receiver-controlled object.

visual.composition: Three actual prototype artifacts show the causal design changes: write became make; send became seal; notification became arrival. Speaker narration supplies the evidence or hypothesis -> conclusion -> requirement -> response chain and explicitly marks participant-dependent conclusions as unverified.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.

Example chain: care already exists -> direct expression may be anticipated as awkward -> the act must feel intentional without demanding a reply -> make one object, give it away and let the receiver control what happens next.
Show only decisions that can be traced to research, critique or an explicit team choice; do not narrate a chronological process diary.

motion.description: Reveal each causal link and its corresponding prototype state in order.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies proposes an ordinary-day ritual—not another social network.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the product as one optional, finite way to express care that already exists.

visual.composition: Product identity, one-sentence mechanism and current Home screen. The mechanism line is: make one appreciation object, give it privately and leave the response to them. Add one restrained dotted branch labelled `FUTURE DIRECTION · UNBUILT · UNTESTED`: a context-aware anti-doomscroll moment could optionally resurface a past note or message, or gently suggest sending something. Keep this visually separate from current prototype proof.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Say that the care already exists and the prototype tests a ritual for expressing it outside an occasion.
Call it a working prototype, not a proven social outcome or validated market need.

The anti-doomscroll direction is optional, unbuilt and untested: context might resurface a past note or message, or gently suggest making something. It is not part of the current prototype demonstration, and it must not shame, interrupt or manipulate users.

future_direction.concept: In a context-aware anti-doomscroll moment, optionally resurface a past note or message, or gently suggest sending something.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity before the home screen.

slides.claim: Make. Seal. Choose how it travels. Give.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the entire sender experience as one finite authored action rather than a feature inventory.

visual.composition: Four-beat live-demo strip: make, seal, choose how it travels, give. Keep only the screens needed to understand those verbs.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Use this as the focused product demo; do not separately narrate every tool, material or animation.
Receiver access by link is the current low-friction prototype direction. Do not claim that sender app, account or production delivery decisions are resolved.

motion.description: Reveal one real product state per spoken verb.

slides.claim: After giving, control passes to the receiver.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the honest receiver contract: choose when to open, then keep, close or remove the prototype object.

visual.composition: Three-beat receiver flow: arrive, open when ready, keep/close/remove. Label browser-local cabinet behaviour as PROTOTYPE rather than ownership, permanence or forever storage.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Use receiver control, revisitable and sender-final language. Avoid own, permanent, immortalised or forever unless the production retention model later proves those claims.
State that production identity, privacy, forwarding, expiry, deletion, persistence and device migration remain unresolved.

motion.description: Reserve the strongest transition for the receiver choosing to open.

slides.claim: We wrote something for you, too.
slides.audience_takeaway: Experience the receiver side voluntarily through a verified QR/link or an equally clear no-device fallback.

visual.composition: A physical-looking handoff card with a clearly labelled placeholder for the verified QR and URL. Include a short visible no-device fallback instruction.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Blocked until a deployed receiver URL is tested on a second device and the real QR replaces the placeholder.
Participation must remain optional, private, generic, accessible and reply-free.
A scan, smile or room reaction demonstrates the flow only; it is not validation.

motion.description: Reveal the card only after the invitation is spoken.

slides.claim: Occasions currently grant permission. Warm & Fuzzies proposes an ordinary-day ritual.
slides.audience_takeaway: Remember the unwritten rule, the mechanism and the unproven proposition in one retellable line.

visual.composition: Return to the occasion-versus-ordinary-day contrast, then close on the firefly and product name. No outcome metric or unsupported norm-change claim.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Close on what the team learned and what the prototype demonstrates, not a claim that the norm has already changed.

motion.description: One social rule, one proposed ritual, one identity lockup.
